AC-06.4.3 and the base-tariff rule say an unmarried employee gets H only if a child lives in the household AND the employee has sole custody or is the main financial contributor. The spec's own evidence disagrees. F-zh-dc0ae9 gives H1N for a child in the household with shared custody, no common household and no alternating custody. F-zh-dc6ace gives H1N for a minor child who does NOT live in the household. F-zh-3eb561 gives H1N for an adult child where the deciding answer is 'pays more than 50%', not 'main contributor'. Which rule should we build for H vs A? We cannot write the derivation or its tests until this is settled.

What exactly does the questionnaire produce as a tariff result, and who sees it? US-06.4 only derives the letter (A/B/C/G/H). But the spec also defines the church-tax suffix (US-06.2), the rule that the digit is the number of counted children, and the Germany cross-border swap (A→L etc.), and AC-06.4.4 says all of these come from the calculator. Should we compute the full tariff code (e.g. H1N, N1Y), only the letter, or nothing? Is the result shown to HR, to the employee, or to neither?

AC-05.3.5 says 'HR can see for each employee whether they are subject'. No story describes what HR sees, where, or when (live while the employee is filling in, or after submission), and the feature puts 'how data is sent to each party' out of scope. Is an HR view of the results (subject yes/no, insurance start date, expected tariff) part of this feature? Should the employee see these derived results?

AC-03.3.1 assumes the first working day 'later changes' after it was recorded. Who changes it, and through what? Can the employee reopen and edit a submitted questionnaire, can HR edit it, or does a new questionnaire go out? Is there a deadline after which changes are no longer accepted? This decides whether we need editing after submission, an HR edit function and an audit of changes.

The flow table says the first working day is 'confirmed if HR already knows it', and AC-03.1.2 says to confirm the date 'as currently agreed'. No story covers HR entering a known date in advance. Does HR pre-fill the first working day (and perhaps the name) before inviting the employee, so the employee only confirms or corrects it? Or does the employee always type it in?

The insurance start rule uses the 'first working day'. If the contract starts on the 1st but the first actual working day is later (weekend or holiday, e.g. contract from Sat 01.06, first day Mon 03.06), the rule gives 01.07 instead of 01.06. Should the rule use the contractual start date or the actual first working day?

New hires often move to Switzerland when they start, or move away from it. Is the home address the current one or the one that applies from the first working day? The country decides source-tax liability, the canton and all the cross-border questions, so the answer changes which questions are asked.

Suppose an employee goes back and changes an earlier answer: the country from Germany to Switzerland, civil status from Married to Single, or the permit to a C permit. Answers they already gave may no longer apply (nationality, spouse data, denomination, children). Under data minimisation, must those answers be thrown away, or may they be kept? Do any rules re-run (e.g. the subject-to-source-tax decision) after submission?

"the employee has entered the country of their home address (address_country) in the home address step" - An internal field identifier appears in the acceptance-criterion prose. Field naming is an engineering choice.

"If it changes, insurance_start_date must be derived again." - A snake_case field/rule identifier is used in the business notes of the First working day item instead of the business term 'insurance start date'.

"It also answers the source tax calculator's civil status question (see rule calculator_civil_status)." - Internal rule ids (calculator_civil_status, and likewise subject_to_source_tax / insurance_start_date in many ACs) are written into the business prose. These are code-style identifiers, not business language.

"the employee can describe each child in its own block (Child 1, Child 2, ...) and can add or remove a child" - This prescribes UI interaction (repeating blocks with add/remove controls) copied from the calculator's screen. The business need is only that each child is described separately.

"| Replacement income (illustrative) | Switzerland | Germany | B permit | Single | Replacement income | – | → | null | not asked | ❌ |" - A programming value ('null') appears as the expected business result where the business term 'no suffix' was meant.

info.message: What does finishing the questionnaire mean for the business? Is there a review/summary step and an explicit submit with a confirmation to the employee? Is HR notified? Can the employee save partway and come back later? None of this is specified, but it decides when HR can rely on the data.

Are there business limits on the first working day, e.g. it must not be in the past or more than N months ahead? Is there a plausibility check on the employee's and spouse's dates of birth (minimum working age)? The pension fund only requires the DD.MM.YYYY format.

Nationality is 'a country by English name'. Which list of nationalities should be offered, and how do stateless employees or employees with unclear status answer? Only 'Switzerland vs not' matters for the rule. (Dual nationality is already listed as an open question.)

AC-03.1.2 ('the question makes clear the date must be the currently agreed one') cannot be tested as written. Is there agreed wording for the question, or a business requirement such as showing the date HR has on file?

In the AC-06.2.3 examples, the replacement-income row gives the result 'null', is marked as failing (❌), and has the denomination column twice. Is the expected result for replacement income 'no suffix'? Please fix the example so it can serve as a test case.

The example tables mix 'required' and 'asked' as expected results for questions that the text says are 'asked and required'. Examples: Canton Zurich 'required' vs St. Gallen 'asked'; the spouse's residence row 'required' vs 'asked'; children 'required' vs 'asked'. Is there a real difference between 'asked' and 'required' (i.e. may some of these be left empty), or are they the same?

The AC-06.4.3 example 'Widowed with an adult child in first education who lives elsewhere → A' leaves out the required 'pays more than 50% of maintenance' answer. Per US-07.5 that answer decides whether the child counts. Which answer is meant, and is the expected digit 0 or 1?

uncited_units.text: HR meeting transcript Everyone and everything here is fictional. Anna is the HR manager at Muster AG. Leo works in product at Lonio.
Can you hear me okay? You're a bit quiet.
Is this better? I'm in the small meeting room, the big one is taken. Sorry, let me just close the door.
Much better. So, thanks for making the time. The idea today is simple. We want your new employees to give us everything once, so that you stop chasing them for
Yes, please. Right now it's a mess. I have a Word document, then an Excel file, and then I type everything into the portals by hand. Last month I spent a full a
Okay. And how many people do you hire in a year?
Around twenty. More in summer. We're about a hundred and fifty people now, mostly here in Zurich.
Good. Let's start with the biggest pain. What takes you the most time?
Okay, that's clear. And the questionnaire itself is what?
Great. Do you also want a photo? Some customers ask for one.
It could. Do you want that from day one?
We're with Pensionskasse Muster. They have a portal, it's quite old. I'll send you some screenshots of it after this call, that's easier than me explaining it.
Perfect. What do you need for the fund that you don't have?
Sorry, one second, someone's at my door. [pause] Okay, I'm back, sorry. Where were we?
The Julia story. It doesn't matter.
Right. What else about the employee affects the fund? Are they married, things like that?
And what are the options in that list?
Okay. Noted. Can I go back to source tax? You said all non-Swiss employees.
Sure, send it if it's easy. Do people need anything from you on the first day? Laptops, things like that? I just want to see if that belongs in the same form.
Okay. Anything else on who needs to do it? I'd rather hear all of it now.
Only the timing. When can we have this?
I'll come back to you on that this week, once we've gone through your screenshots.
Good. I'll send them after lunch. Thanks, Leo.

open_questions.question: How should an employee in a registered partnership answer civil status, and do the pension fund and the source tax spouse exemption treat them like married employees (partner's date of birth, partner's nationality/permit/residence)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The pension fund list (Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed) has no registered partnership, but the calculator groups it with married, and such employees exist (Daniel). Without an answer they cannot be registered correctly.
options: Ask them to choose 'Married' and treat them as married everywhere
Ask the pension fund how to register them and keep a separate answer for source tax
Ask HR to handle it manually
open_questions.recommendation: Ask Pensionskasse Muster via HR. Until then, treat registered partners as Married for both parties, because the calculator explicitly groups them together.

open_questions.question: Which civil status should a separated (still married) employee choose? The calculator groups 'separated' with single, but the pension fund has no such option.
open_questions.why_it_matters: A separated employee would pick Married for the pension fund and get the married source tax path, which may differ from the calculator's grouping.
options: Married for the pension fund, plus an extra 'separated' question for source tax only
open_questions.recommendation: Confirm with HR. Do not add a question until then.

open_questions.question: Does the pension fund ask for any spouse data when civil status is Divorced or Widowed?
open_questions.why_it_matters: No screenshot shows these cases. Asking too little could block the registration.
options: Spouse's date of birth also appears
open_questions.recommendation: Assume no extra fields. Verify with a screenshot of these two cases.

open_questions.question: Does the pension fund's 'Canton' mean canton of residence or of work, and what is entered for employees who live abroad (Germany, Liechtenstein)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The field is required, but the list only has the 26 Swiss cantons. Cross-border employees could not be registered.
options: Canton of residence; ask the fund what to enter for residents abroad
Canton of work (e.g. Zurich), so it is not asked of the employee
open_questions.recommendation: Ask Pensionskasse Muster. Meanwhile ask the canton only of Swiss residents.

open_questions.question: Which permit types should the employee and spouse be able to choose from, and how does a spouse without any permit answer?
open_questions.why_it_matters: No source lists the permits. Only 'C permit' changes the outcome, but the employee needs a list they recognise.
open_questions.recommendation: Ask HR for the list it uses. The rule only needs to tell C permit apart from other permits.

open_questions.question: Is the consolidated source tax rule complete and does 'here' mean Switzerland? HR hedged ('I think so') before adding further conditions.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The rule decides who sees the whole source tax section and the spouse questions. A wrong rule asks Swiss employees too much or misses people who are subject.
open_questions.recommendation: Have HR confirm the decision table of subject_to_source_tax.

open_questions.question: How should employees with several nationalities, one of them Swiss, answer the nationality question?
open_questions.why_it_matters: HR's rule is 'Swiss passport'. Dual nationals could pick their other nationality and be wrongly sent the source tax questions.
options: Ask 'Do you hold Swiss citizenship?' first
open_questions.recommendation: Confirm with HR that any Swiss citizenship counts as Swiss.

open_questions.question: Is a new employee's income always earned income (Erwerbseinkommen), so the income-type question can be fixed instead of asked?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Asking a new hire about replacement income is confusing and collects unnecessary data. Fixing it also removes the replacement-income cross-border variants.
open_questions.recommendation: Fix to earned income by product decision. Until then it is modelled as asked.

open_questions.question: HR says everyone living abroad is subject to source tax, but the calculator can return 'in principle no source tax liability' for Liechtenstein residents. Which result counts?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It affects what HR does after the questionnaire. It does not change which questions are asked.
open_questions.recommendation: Keep asking these employees all source tax questions and let the calculator result decide. Confirm with HR.

open_questions.question: Can a new employee answer 'certificate of residence provided' and 'proof of more than 60 non-return days provided' before starting? To whom are these documents provided?
open_questions.why_it_matters: These questions ask about documents, possibly the 'German forms' HR mentioned. The employee may not have them yet.
options: Ask as yes/no and let HR collect the documents
Ask whether the employee will provide them
open_questions.recommendation: Ask HR how this works today for Stefan.

open_questions.question: Do the child and cross-border paths behave as modelled for every combination? The calculator was only spot-checked for A/B/H cross-border tariffs, more than 3 children, deleting children and special tariffs (e.g. D).
open_questions.why_it_matters: Untested paths could need more questions.
open_questions.recommendation: Accept for the questionnaire (the question conditions are explicit). Explore further only if the tariff is computed by Lonio.

open_questions.question: Should the questionnaire remind employees to bring their permit on the first day, and with which wording?
open_questions.why_it_matters: HR asked for it, but Leo deferred the wording, so it is undecided.
options: Add a reminder for non-Swiss employees
open_questions.recommendation: Product owner to decide. It adds no data collection.

open_questions.question: Should the spouse's residence be asked as a country or only as 'lives in Switzerland: yes/no'?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Only whether the spouse lives in Switzerland matters, and data minimisation favours the narrower question.
open_questions.recommendation: Ask yes/no 'Does your spouse live in Switzerland?' if the product owner agrees.

questions.question: AC-06.4.3 and the base-tariff rule say an unmarried employee gets H only if a child lives in the household AND the employee has sole custody or is the main financial contributor. The spec's own evidence disagrees. F-zh-dc0ae9 gives H1N for a child in the household with shared custody, no common household and no alternating custody. F-zh-dc6ace gives H1N for a minor child who does NOT live in the household. F-zh-3eb561 gives H1N for an adult child where the deciding answer is 'pays more than 50%', not 'main contributor'. Which rule should we build for H vs A? We cannot write the derivation or its tests until this is settled.

What exactly does the questionnaire produce as a tariff result, and who sees it? US-06.4 only derives the letter (A/B/C/G/H). But the spec also defines the church-tax suffix (US-06.2), the rule that the digit is the number of counted children, and the Germany cross-border swap (A→L etc.), and AC-06.4.4 says all of these come from the calculator. Should we compute the full tariff code (e.g. H1N, N1Y), only the letter, or nothing? Is the result shown to HR, to the employee, or to neither?

AC-05.3.5 says 'HR can see for each employee whether they are subject'. No story describes what HR sees, where, or when (live while the employee is filling in, or after submission), and the feature puts 'how data is sent to each party' out of scope. Is an HR view of the results (subject yes/no, insurance start date, expected tariff) part of this feature? Should the employee see these derived results?

AC-03.3.1 assumes the first working day 'later changes' after it was recorded. Who changes it, and through what? Can the employee reopen and edit a submitted questionnaire, can HR edit it, or does a new questionnaire go out? Is there a deadline after which changes are no longer accepted? This decides whether we need editing after submission, an HR edit function and an audit of changes.

The flow table says the first working day is 'confirmed if HR already knows it', and AC-03.1.2 says to confirm the date 'as currently agreed'. No story covers HR entering a known date in advance. Does HR pre-fill the first working day (and perhaps the name) before inviting the employee, so the employee only confirms or corrects it? Or does the employee always type it in?

The insurance start rule uses the 'first working day'. If the contract starts on the 1st but the first actual working day is later (weekend or holiday, e.g. contract from Sat 01.06, first day Mon 03.06), the rule gives 01.07 instead of 01.06. Should the rule use the contractual start date or the actual first working day?

New hires often move to Switzerland when they start, or move away from it. Is the home address the current one or the one that applies from the first working day? The country decides source-tax liability, the canton and all the cross-border questions, so the answer changes which questions are asked.

Suppose an employee goes back and changes an earlier answer: the country from Germany to Switzerland, civil status from Married to Single, or the permit to a C permit. Answers they already gave may no longer apply (nationality, spouse data, denomination, children). Under data minimisation, must those answers be thrown away, or may they be kept? Do any rules re-run (e.g. the subject-to-source-tax decision) after submission?

What does finishing the questionnaire mean for the business? Is there a review/summary step and an explicit submit with a confirmation to the employee? Is HR notified? Can the employee save partway and come back later? None of this is specified, but it decides when HR can rely on the data.

Are there business limits on the first working day, e.g. it must not be in the past or more than N months ahead? Is there a plausibility check on the employee's and spouse's dates of birth (minimum working age)? The pension fund only requires the DD.MM.YYYY format.

Nationality is 'a country by English name'. Which list of nationalities should be offered, and how do stateless employees or employees with unclear status answer? Only 'Switzerland vs not' matters for the rule. (Dual nationality is already listed as an open question.)

AC-03.1.2 ('the question makes clear the date must be the currently agreed one') cannot be tested as written. Is there agreed wording for the question, or a business requirement such as showing the date HR has on file?

In the AC-06.2.3 examples, the replacement-income row gives the result 'null', is marked as failing (❌), and has the denomination column twice. Is the expected result for replacement income 'no suffix'? Please fix the example so it can serve as a test case.

The example tables mix 'required' and 'asked' as expected results for questions that the text says are 'asked and required'. Examples: Canton Zurich 'required' vs St. Gallen 'asked'; the spouse's residence row 'required' vs 'asked'; children 'required' vs 'asked'. Is there a real difference between 'asked' and 'required' (i.e. may some of these be left empty), or are they the same?

The AC-06.4.3 example 'Widowed with an adult child in first education who lives elsewhere → A' leaves out the required 'pays more than 50% of maintenance' answer. Per US-07.5 that answer decides whether the child counts. Which answer is meant, and is the expected digit 0 or 1?

review.summary: Not ready. One example fails (AC-06.2.3 replacement income, 'null' vs None). Two open questions are blocking (OQ-registered-partnership, OQ-canton). The tariff-letter rule contradicts the spec's own evidence. Several major dev-refinement questions have no answer: scope of the tariff result and HR view, post-submission edits, and HR pre-fill. Internal identifiers leak into business prose. Many items and stories are inferred, and some trace judgements are only partial.

findings.title: Failing example: replacement-income church tax suffix
findings.why: The example is the only failed simulation. It expects the programming value 'null' where the business meaning is 'no suffix'. The row is also marked ❌ and repeats the denomination column.
findings.evidence: examples AC-06.2.3 / Replacement income: church_tax_suffix = None, expected 'null'. tech_leak and dev_refinement on US-06.2.
findings.action: Rewrite the expected result as 'no suffix' and define it unambiguously, e.g. empty. Remove the duplicate column and the ❌, then re-run the examples.

findings.title: Base tariff H vs A rule contradicts its own evidence
findings.why: AC-06.4.3 and rule.base_tariff_letter say H requires the child in the household plus sole custody or main contributor. Three cited facts give H1N in cases that rule excludes. The derivation and its tests cannot be written until this is settled.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement US-06.4 (major). Facts F-zh_source_tax_calculator-dc0ae9, -dc6ace, -3eb561. trace_judge on rule.base_tariff_letter. The widowed adult-child example omits the '>50% maintenance' answer.
findings.action: Add a decision in decisions.yaml on the exact H vs A conditions. This could be 'counted child' rather than household plus custody. Fix AC-06.4.3 and its examples to match, including the digit 0 or 1.

findings.title: Blocking open question: registered partnership
findings.why: Employees in a registered partnership (e.g. Daniel) cannot be registered correctly. The pension fund list has no such status, and the question affects the spouse data and the source-tax exemption.
findings.evidence: OQ-registered-partnership (blocking: true). It affects civil_status, the spouse items, subject_to_source_tax and calculator_civil_status. OQ-separated is related.
findings.action: Ask Pensionskasse Muster through HR. Record a decision. The interim recommendation is to treat registered partners as Married, with OQ-separated resolved consistently.

findings.title: Blocking open question: pension fund 'Canton' meaning
findings.why: It is unknown whether the canton means residence or work, and what to enter for cross-border employees. The field is required and the list has only Swiss cantons. residence_canton is also named and described as the canton of residence without backing.
findings.evidence: OQ-canton (blocking: true). fact_judge on F-pension_portal-b359c3. trace_judge on item.residence_canton. US-02.4.
findings.action: Get the fund's answer and decide what is entered for residents of Germany and Liechtenstein. Rename or reword the item to match.

findings.title: Scope of the tariff output and HR visibility undefined
findings.why: The spec derives only the tariff letter. It also defines the suffix, the digit and the cross-border swap, and says HR can see results. It never says what is computed, who sees it, or when. Engineering cannot size the feature without this.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement US-06.4 (major) and US-05.3 AC-05.3.5 (major). US-01.1 (minor, submit and notify flow).
findings.action: Add a decision on the output. Is it the full code, only the letter or nothing? Who sees it? What are the submit and notify semantics? Update the stories or move HR visibility out of scope explicitly.

findings.title: Post-submission changes and answer invalidation unspecified
findings.why: US-03.3 assumes the first working day changes later, but no actor or mechanism is defined. Going back and changing earlier answers can orphan data that data minimisation forbids keeping.
findings.action: Decide who can edit and until when. Decide whether dependent answers are discarded when upstream answers change. Add ACs for both.

findings.title: First working day inputs and start-date rule ambiguous
findings.why: No story covers HR pre-filling the date. Using the actual first working day instead of the contractual start can push the insurance start to the wrong month. The residence-address timing (current vs at start) changes which questions are asked.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement US-03.1 (major), feature.md insurance rule (major), US-02.3 (major). AC-03.1.2 is untestable as written.
findings.action: Decide whether the date is pre-filled by HR. Decide whether the rule uses the contract start or the first working day, and whether the address is current or as at the start date. Add testable wording.

findings.title: Item expressions and business text do not match their trace
findings.why: Several required_when and asked_when expressions contradict their own business text. Some claims have no cited fact: the 'only if subject' condition, the step order, the Germany/Liechtenstein rows citing missing facts, and the 'sensitive data' note. A developer would build from the expressions.
findings.evidence: trace_judge: spouse_permit_type, has_children, confession, income_type, civil_status, calculator_residence, questionnaire_flow, US-01.2, US-02.4, US-06.1 to US-06.3.
findings.action: Align each expression with its text. Cite the missing hr_transcript facts, or mark the items as decisions. Drop or confirm the unbacked claims.

findings.title: Source-tax rule only partly confirmed
findings.why: The rule decides who sees the whole source-tax section. Anna hedged, and 'here' meaning Switzerland is an assumption. The Liechtenstein result conflicts with HR's 'always subject'. Income type is still modelled as asked.
findings.evidence: OQ-source-tax-rule, OQ-liechtenstein, OQ-income-type. fact_judge on F-hr_transcript-550840 and -5af8d0.
findings.action: Have HR confirm the decision table. Record the product decisions on income type (fixed to earned income) and on which Liechtenstein result counts.

findings.title: Technical identifiers leak into business prose
findings.why: Field and rule ids and UI mechanics appear in acceptance criteria and notes, which turns engineering choices into spec content.
findings.evidence: tech_leak: US-08.1 (address_country), feature.md (insurance_start_date, calculator_civil_status), US-07.2 (Child 1/2 blocks with add/remove).
findings.action: Replace the ids with business terms. State only the need that each child is described separately.
